chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abu al-Khattab said, on the authority of Ali ibn Asbat, that he asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him)

about ability (al-istita'ah), so he said: 'A servant is capable when he possesses four characteristics: his route is free from trouble, his body is healthy, he has all his limbs, and has a means of sustenance provided to him by Allah, the Mighty and High.' I said: 'May I be your ransom! Explain these reasons for me.' He said: 'In order to be capable, a servant needs to have a route free from trouble. He needs to have a healthy body. And he needs to have all his limbs. He may intend to fornicate, but at first he does not find a woman then he finds one. Then, either he would be protected by Allah and he would stop from it as Yusuf (peace be upon him) did; or Allah would abandon him between him and his intentions. Thus, he would fornicate and would be labeled a fornicator. He has not obeyed Allah from compulsion, and did not disobey because he was coerced.'
ai.seo_question: What are the four conditions for a servant's ability (istita'ah) according to Imam al-Rida (AS)?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies that human 'ability' (istita'ah) is not merely physical capacity but a nuanced state where divine decree either protects the servant from sin or allows their free will to manifest, as illustrated by the example of Prophet Yusuf. This hadith is pivotal in Shia theological debates regarding *al-Jabr wa al-Tafwid* (compulsion vs. delegation), affirming that God’s foreknowledge and decree do not coerce the individual’s choice. It underscores the balance between divine power and human responsibility, a core tenet of Shia *Usul al-Din*.
